[[File:Academician Ildar Ibragimov.jpg|thumb|Ildar Abdulovich Ibragimov in 2015]]
'''Ildar Abdulovich Ibragimov''' (Ильдар Абдулович Ибрагимов, born 15 July 1932, [[Saint Petersburg|Leningrad]]) is a Russian mathematician, specializing in probability theory and mathematical statistics.<ref>[[Peter J. Bickel]], [[Lucien Le Cam]] ''A conversation with Ildar Ibragimov'', Statistical Science, vol. 5, 1990, pp. 347–355 {{JSTOR|2245822}}</ref>

==Biography==
Ibragimov is the son of a father who was an engineer with [[Bashkirs|Bashkir]] ancestry and a mother who was a physician from a [[Tatars|Tatar]] family with origins in Kazan. Ildar Ibragimov studied at  [[Saint Petersburg State University|Leningrad State University]], where he graduated in mathematics in 1956. He received in 1960 his Russian candidate degree (Ph.D.) under [[Yuri Linnik]]<ref name=MathGen>{{MathGenealogy|id=51539|name=Ildar Abdullovich Ibragimov}}</ref> and in 1967 his Russian doctorate (higher doctoral degree). In 1969 he became a professor of probability at Leningrad State University.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Bickel |first=Peter J. |last2=Le Cam |first2=Lucien |date=1990 |title=A Conversation with Ildar Ibragimov |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/2245822 |journal=Statistical Science |volume=5 |issue=3 |pages=347–355 |issn=0883-4237}}</ref>

He is a senior scientist and director of the laboratory of statistical methods  at the [[Steklov Institute]] in [[Saint Petersburg]], a position he has held there since 1972 as the successor to Yuri Linnik. Ibragimov was elected in 1990 a corresponding member and in 1997 a full member of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]]. In 1970 he received the [[Lenin Prize]]. In 1989 he was the Wald Lecturer of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]]. In 1966 in Moscow he was an Invited Speaker of the [[International Congress of Mathematicians|ICM]].<ref>{{cite book|editor=Aizerman, M. A.|author=Ibragimov, I. A.|chapter=Some aspects of spectral theory of stationary processes|title=Thirty-one invited addresses at the International Congress of Mathematicians in Moscow in 1966|series=American Mathematical Society Translations, Series 2, Vol. 70|pages=57–65|publisher=American Mathematical Soc.|year=1968|isbn=9780821896457|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=3xQpXJ_hmBMC}}</ref>

His doctoral students include [[Taivo Arak]] and [[Boris Tsirelson]].<ref name=MathGen/>

==Selected publications==
*with Linnik: ''Independent and stationary sequences of random variables'', Groningen, Wolters-Noordhoff 1971
*with Y. A. Rozanov: ''Gaussian Random Processes'', Springer Verlag 1978<ref>{{cite journal|title=Review of ''Gaussian random processes'' by I. A. Ibragimov and Yu. A. Rozanov|author=Dudley, R. M.|authorlink=Richard M. Dudley|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=2|issue=2|year=1980|pages=373–378|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1980-14768-0|doi-access=free}}</ref>
*with R. Z. Hasminskii: ''Statistical estimation, asymptotic theory'', Springer Verlag 1981<ref>{{cite journal|author=Le Cam, Lucien|title=Review of: ''Statistical estimation, asymptotic theory'' by I. A. Ibragimov and R. Z. Has'minskii and ''Contributions to a general asymptotic statistical theory'' by J. Pfanzagl|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc.|volume=11|issue=2|year=1984|pages=392–400|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1984-15326-6|doi-access=free}}</ref>
*as editor with A. Yu. Zaitzev: ''Probability theory and mathematical statistics'', Gordon and Breach 1996
*as editor with N. Balakrishnan, V. B. Nevzorov: ''Asymptotic methods in probability and statistics with applications'', Birkhäuser 2001
